// anikit:aa off
void mainImage(out vec4 o, in vec2 f){ vec2 uv = f/iResolution.xy; vec2 q = uv - vec2(0.62, 0.5); float v = 1.0 - 0.55*dot(q*vec2(1.6, 1.0), q*vec2(1.6, 1.0)); float g = fract(sin(dot(floor(f) + floor(iTime*24.0), vec2(12.9898, 78.233)))*43758.5453) - 0.5; vec3 c = vec3(0.039, 0.059, 0.090)*(0.75 + 0.45*v) + g*0.012; o = vec4(c, 1.0); }

layers.text: Source: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, Mauna Loa Observatory, monthly mean CO₂ (ppm), Mar 1958 – Sep 2026

Every year,
the planet
takes a breath.

Each spring the northern forests leaf out
and pull carbon from the air. From May to
September, carbon dioxide falls by about 6 ppm.
In winter, it all comes back.

Each loop is a year.
Each sits a little
further out.

Monthly mean, plotted as a clock:
angle is the month, distance
from the centre is carbon dioxide.

The breath hasn’t changed.
The air has.

Carbon dioxide now rises 2.6 ppm a year, 3.2× the pace of the 1960s.
ppm per year, by decade (trend of the deseasonalised series).
